title: Behind the Scenes: Riot Rookie
transcript_text: My name is Faustus Othello. Yeah, my name is Hannah Crawford. My name is Joshua Musinera. My name is Tiffany Guerrero. I'm an operations intern. I am the Learning and Development Intern. I'm the electrical engineer. My role right now is an HR intern. Personally, I've really grown through this because it's one of these experiences that are outside of the institutions. So I've finally been able to apply all the engineering that I learned previously. Especially, I definitely say, because I was the role that I was doing. I got to work a lot with leadership. And so I got a lot of exposure to people who are actually leading teams, managing teams, which is something I would like to do in the future. And so I think just having that professional guidance and advice that I got from them, they're out the interviews that I was doing with them and working with them, was really helped me grow professionally. This experience has been amazing to help me grow both professionally and personally. Professionally, I've learned to be on a full site with people and not just being in the classroom and working on theories. I've had to talk to people and things don't come automatically. There's lead time, you have to order things. So it's helped me learn real world applications. This is my first time working a full-time job. So this internship has really opened my eyes with the working full-time with just a culture that is amazing. The obviously, it's always a good time. And I think that's why I really do, I do the commute of an hour. I look forward to seeing who I'm working with on a day-to-day basis. They keep it really positive. Make sure that everyone is good. Everyone helps each other out in any way possible. And so I think just very giving department in general. I also think all the departments here are structured in that way. I have loved that they have just really embraced me and not forced me but really pushed me to make those connections. And they are so funny. Every single day, I'm just laughing so much because they are so funny. And so it's just been a connection that I've got to make with them. They said going on, they want to be a mentor for me throughout my career. And so then taking the time and the effort to make those connections with me has been so amazing. I would say the thing that I enjoy most is the people. Honestly, it's been great seeing all the electrical components and all the bells and whistles and the substations and the miners. But honestly, at the end of the day, 20 years from now, I won't be talking about the substations. I'll be talking about my supervisor. I'll be talking about the people that I worked with and that's who's really made an impact on me. I have never worked with a company with this many genuine people. There was never a day I never did not want to come into work. I was always looking forward to coming in. Everyone is so nice, so genuine. I was even a part of this little volleyball team that we played almost every Monday. I got to play maybe four or five games with them. So just connecting with them on a deeper level and even though I'm probably younger, they never treated me like I was a kid. And so that was really important to me as well. It drives to make an impact at such a vast pace. I think the people here are always open to seeing someone put in their work and representing that throughout the internship. I would tell them to scale themselves. I think that's one of the biggest thing is kind of coming in. I felt like I had to, or I wanted to give off this portrayal being super smart and knowing everything and having a bunch of background. And that's not necessarily you don't have to be that way. You can come in not knowing everything, but wanting to learn everything. Richard Wright interns, I would say, talk less and listen more. People have a lot to teach you. And I would say don't get stuck in your department as a silo. Go talk to people in HR. Go talk to the frontline workers. Get a full view of it. Visit multiple facilities. Visit Corsicana. Visit Rockdale. Go to Austin. Don't be afraid to slack people. Jason's a great CEO. He's very well to me. You'll be happy to talk to you. So everyone from the CEO to the frontline, it's an open door policy. And don't be afraid to ask questions and most importantly, listen more than you speak. I thought someone was going to come in and tell me do this, this, this, this, at this time of day. But I had to learn that they trust their interns and they want their interns to pull the reins and learn from them, from Riot, but also learn at their own pace and learn how the business industry works.
